title: Local perfect lifting from a lisse residue complex without finite coefficient hypotheses
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], meaning that it has a finite affine open cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, $J\subseteq A$ an ideal, and assume $A\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_{n\geq1}A/J^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. On the small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $B_X=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}\underline{A/J^n}$, using constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Use module sheaves and derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and let $M\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_X))$ be locally derived $JB_X$-complete [def-weil-pbc-locally-derived-ringed-ideal-complete]. Suppose $M\otimes^L_{B_X}\underline{A/J}\simeq
u_X^*C$, where $
u_X$ is the étale/pro-étale comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and $C$ is a bounded étale $A/J$-complex. Assume each $H^q(C)$ is étale locally constant with finitely generated $A/J$-module values [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and that there are integers $a\leq b$ with $H^q(C\otimes^L_{\underline{A/J}}N)=0$ for every degree-zero étale $A/J$-module sheaf $N$ and every $q
otin[a,b]$. Derived tensors are [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Then there is a pro-étale covering $\{U_t	o X\}$ and, for each $t$, a bounded complex $P_t^ ullet$ of finite projective $A$-modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex] such that $M|_{U_t}\simeq (B_X|_{U_t})\otimes_A P_t^ ullet$. The last expression is termwise extension of the constant complex. Neither $A/J$ nor $A/J^n$ is required to be finite as a set or perfect over $A$.

source.place: Tag 09C6, lemma-connected-adic-lisse; passage between constant and completed coefficients in Tag 099L, section-derived-completion-noetherian. Bhatt–Scholze, literature/bhatt-scholze-pro-etale-topology_arXiv-1309.1198.pdf, Lemma 6.6.8 and the forward proof of Proposition 6.6.11; apply on the finitely many connected open components of affine Noetherian charts.

proof.text: Choose generators of $J$, possible since $A$ is Noetherian, and put $N=\operatorname{Res}_{\underline A}M$. The constant/completed coefficient equivalence applies on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$: its completed ring is exactly $B_X$, its completeness notion is the local one in the statement, and it identifies the reductions of $N$ and $M$ compatibly with all quotient maps. The residue complex $C$ is constructible, using the single stratum $X$ for each of its finitely many nonzero locally constant cohomology sheaves. Apply the finite-reduction structure lemma to $N,C,[a,b]$. Write $A_n=A/J^n$, $M_n=M\otimes^L_{B_X}\underline{A_n}$, and obtain étale $C_n$ with bounded constructible cohomology and Tor amplitude $[a,b]$, and compatible $\alpha_n,\beta_n$. In particular $M$ is the derived limit of this specified quotient tower after restricting scalars. No perfectness of $A_n$ over $A$ was invoked.

source.place: Tags 099L, 099M and 09C2; opening of the proof of Tag 09C6

proof.text: Work on a connected clopen component $Y$ of an affine Noetherian chart of $X$. These form an open covering. Indeed the underlying affine space is Noetherian by the cited lemma; Noetherian induction on closed subsets gives finitely many irreducible components (a minimal counterexample would be reducible into two smaller closed subsets). Grouping those finitely many components by chains of nonempty intersections gives finitely many connected components; each group and its complement are finite unions of closed components, hence clopen. Slice restriction is identified with the pro-étale site of $Y$ by the localization lemma. It is sectionwise restriction, so preserves products and kernels, and it preserves epimorphisms because their locally lifting sections lift over the same covering in the slice. It is therefore exact. It preserves constant sheaves and their inverse limits. Countable products are exact and represent derived products; consequently restriction takes the quotient Roos triangle, including its completion unit, to the same triangle on $Y$. Thus $M|_Y$ and $N|_Y$ remain complete and have the restricted compatible quotient tower. Restriction also commutes with the total tensor calculation on K-flat resolutions. Apply the finite-reduction structure lemma on $Y$, choosing these restricted markings, and henceforth replace $X$ by nonempty connected affine $Y$.

source.place: Tag 09C6, connected-local reduction; Tags 099M and 0947 for restriction of completion

proof.text: For each $n$, apply nilpotent-reduction lissity on the étale site with coefficient ring $A_n$, ideal $J/J^n$, and bounded complex $C_n$. The ideal is nilpotent, $A_n$ is Noetherian (ideals correspond to ideals of $A$ containing $J^n$), and the normalized reduction of $C_n$ modulo $J/J^n$ is $C_1=C$. Thus all cohomology sheaves of $C_n$ are étale locally constant of finite type. The connected étale perfect-constancy lemma now applies: the Tor bound and boundedness were provided in step 1. Fix one geometric point $\bar x$ of $Y$ and put $E_n=(C_n)_{\bar x}$. It gives a perfect $E_n$ and one étale local constant value $E_n$ for $C_n$. Take the exact stalk of $\beta_n$. The tensor-pullback comparison gives normalizations $E_{n+1}\otimes^L_{A_{n+1}}A_n\simeq E_n$. Define the transition $E_{n+1}\to E_n$ as the scalar-extension unit followed by this normalization, considered first in $D(A_{n+1})$ and then in $D(A)$. On K-flat representatives the unit is $p\mapsto p\otimes1$ and reassociation is $(p\otimes u)\otimes v\mapsto p\otimes uv$; hence the stalk normalizations have the same quotient cocycles as the $\beta_n$.

Apply algebraic perfect inverse-limit reconstruction to the tower $E_n$ with those transitions. Its ring hypothesis is the given $A\simeq\varprojlim A/J^n$, and $E_1$ is perfect by step 3. Obtain a perfect $P\in D(A)$ and projection-induced isomorphisms $P\otimes_A^L A_n\simeq E_n$ compatible with all transitions. Choose a bounded finite-projective representative $P^\bullet$. Next take an affine weakly contractible pro-étale covering $\{W_t\to Y\}$. The weakly contractible clause of the connected perfect-constancy lemma gives, for each $n$ and each $W=W_t$, an isomorphism $M_n|_W\simeq\underline{E_n}|_W\simeq\underline{P^\bullet\otimes_A A_n}|_W$. These isomorphisms need not be compatible, and no such compatibility is presumed in the next step. For every such $W$, the localization lemma identifies $Y_{\mathrm{proét}}/W$ with $W_{\mathrm{proét}}$. Restriction is exact, preserves sectionwise products and the finite Koszul tensor complexes, and therefore preserves their Roos completion unit, since countable products are exact. Hence $M|_W$ is locally derived complete, and restriction of the completed coefficient ring is $B_Y|_W=\varprojlim_n\underline{A_n}|_W$; this justifies the completion calculation on $W$ below.

source.place: Tag 09C6, algebraic reconstruction by Tag 09AW, and the choice of weakly contractible cover

proof.text: Fix $W$ and write $B=B_X|_W$, $T=B\otimes_A P^\bullet$, and $T_n=\underline{P^\bullet\otimes_A A_n}|_W$. Every term of $T$ is the image of an idempotent on a finite power of $B$. In fact it is the inverse limit of the corresponding idempotent summands of $\underline{A_n}^{\,r}$, since an image of an idempotent is the equalizer of that idempotent and the identity. These summands are killed by $J^n$. The torsion-limit completeness theorem makes $T$ complete after restriction to $\underline A$, and the constant/completed equivalence makes it complete over $B$. Put $P^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(P^\bullet,A)$, with degree $i$ term $\operatorname{Hom}_A(P^{-i},A)$ and differential $(-1)^{i+1}$ times precomposition by $d_P$. Set $H=(B\otimes_A P^\vee)\otimes_B^L M|_W$. A finite-projective term is a retract of a finite free term, so its tensor is exact; a bounded such complex is K-flat. Its tensor with a product is the product of its tensors: each total degree has only finitely many summands, and for an idempotent $e$ on a finite free module, its image commutes with products because $\operatorname{im}(e)=\ker(1-e)$ and products commute with kernels and finite powers. Thus tensoring the quotient-completion Roos triangle of $M|_W$ with this bounded dual identifies $H\simeq R\lim_n H_n$, where $H_n=T_n^\vee\otimes_{\underline{A_n}}^L M_n|_W$ are its canonical reductions. The coefficient-completion lemma identifies this quotient-limit unit with the local completeness unit, so $H$ is locally complete. By step 4 every $H_n$ is a constant complex with value $(P^\vee\otimes_A A_n)\otimes_{A_n}(P^\bullet\otimes_A A_n)$. This is perfect, in particular at $n=1$.

source.place: Tag 09C6, the dual complex and H_n; fills the completeness and reduction details omitted there

proof.text: For clarity the degree-zero cohomology groups $G_n=H^0(W,H_n)$ are precisely $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(W_{\mathrm{proét}},A_n)}(T_n,M_n|_W)$. Evaluation on $W$ is exact. The sheaf $\underline{A_n}$ is therefore projective in the slice module category, since its Hom functor is evaluation; each term of $T_n$ is a finite direct summand of such free sheaves and is projective too. Bounded-above projective complexes are K-projective, so the derived-Hom bijection identifies these morphisms with chain maps modulo chain homotopy. Termwise finite-projective duality identifies their Hom complex with $T_n^\vee\otimes M_n|_W$: on a summand of $A_n^r$ the map is $\lambda\otimes m\mapsto(p\mapsto\lambda(p)m)$; for complexes use the displayed dual differential and the usual tensor sign. Over $B$, exact evaluation gives $\operatorname{Hom}_B(B,F)=F(W)$, so the finite direct summands of finite free $B$-sheaves in $T$ are projective. The two cited K-projective statements then identify $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(T,M|_W)$ with $H^0$ of the global Hom complex. Evaluation $\lambda\otimes m\mapsto(p\mapsto\lambda(p)m)$, with the dual differential of step 5, identifies that complex with the sections of a representative of $H$; exact evaluation identifies its cohomology with $H^0(W,H)$. These identifications commute with quotient reduction because the evaluation formula and both differentials commute with the coefficient map $A_{n+1}\to A_n$. Apply the weakly contractible ML lemma to $\operatorname{Res}H$. Its reductions are the $H_n$ by coefficient comparison, it is complete by step 5, and its first constant value is perfect. Therefore the tower $G_n$ has eventually stable images. Each $G_n$ contains an isomorphism by step 4.

source.place: Tag 09C6, application of Tag 09C5; explicit identification of sections with actual derived morphisms

proof.text: Let $S_n=\bigcap_{k\geq n}\operatorname{im}(G_k\to G_n)$. The ML property says that this intersection is an eventual image. The maps $S_{n+1}\to S_n$ are surjective: for fixed $n$, choose $k$ beyond stabilization at both $n$ and $n+1$ and lift an element of $S_n$ from $G_k$. Choose $k$ beyond stabilization at $1$ and an isomorphism in $G_k$; its reduction $g_1\in S_1$ is an isomorphism. Repeatedly lift along the surjections $S_{n+1}\to S_n$ to obtain a compatible sequence $(g_n)$ beginning with $g_1$. Equivalently apply the nonempty-ML-limit lemma to the fibers over $g_1$ in the stable systems. Apply the sheaf Milnor sequence to the strict quotient tower $H_n$. The Roos model is a derived limit by exact countable products. Exact evaluation at $W$ preserves the resulting epimorphism $H^0(H)\twoheadrightarrow\lim_nH^0(H_n)$, and evaluation commutes with the limit sectionwise. Thus $(g_n)$ lifts to a class in $H^0(W,H)$, hence by step 6 to an actual morphism $g:T\to M|_W$ of $B$-complexes. Its derived reduction modulo $J$ is $g_1$, an isomorphism. This constructs the compatible map; it does not take a nonfunctorial limit of independently chosen isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 09C6, stable-image argument and the compatible maps; Tag 0947 Milnor sequence

proof.text: Let $Q=\operatorname{Cone}(g)$. Local completeness is closed under cones: the Koszul-completion unit in the constant/completed lemma is a natural map between exact functors (finite Koszul tensor and the exact derived-limit functor); its cone vanishes at the third vertex whenever it vanishes at the other two, by the long exact cohomology sequence. Since both $T$ and $M|_W$ are complete, $Q$ is complete. Its first reduction is zero. All its reductions are zero: the exact constant sequence $0\to J^n/J^{n+1}\to A/J^{n+1}\to A/J^n\to0$ gives after derived tensor with $\operatorname{Res}Q$ a triangle whose first term is $(Q\otimes_B^L\underline{A/J})\otimes_{\underline{A/J}}^L\underline{J^n/J^{n+1}}=0$. Induction from $n=1$ proves the claim. Constant realization is exact; derived scalar extension preserves this triangle, and reassociation is the balancing map already written in step 3. Completeness therefore gives $Q\simeq R\lim_n0=0$. The long exact cohomology sequence shows $g$ is an isomorphism. On each $W_t$ we have proved exactly $M|_{W_t}\simeq (B_X|_{W_t})\otimes_A P^\bullet$. The tensor is computed termwise because the finite-projective terms are flat and the complex is bounded. Assemble the covers over all connected affine components of the original $X$. If $X$ is empty take the empty cover. All coefficient rings remain the original $A$ and its quotients; neither finiteness as sets nor quotient perfectness was used.

tool_uses.why: Step 7 uses the stated epimorphism from degree-zero cohomology of the sequential derived limit to the limit of degree-zero cohomology sheaves. This is a generic pro-etale homological tool, not a replacement for the integral-model route.
Steps 5 and 8 use bounded complexes of flat modules being K-flat to compute the displayed tensors termwise. No local-lifting conclusion is taken from this generic tool.
The steps use K-flat scalar extension, preservation of coefficient triangles, and tensor reassociation; the unit does not restate this general ringed-site operation.
Steps 2 and 7 use termwise products representing derived products when countable products are exact, so restriction and the Roos construction have the asserted derived meaning.
Steps 1, 2, 5, 6 and 8 use the equivalence on complete objects and its compatible quotient and completion-unit comparisons; it is used for arbitrary Noetherian coefficients, exactly as stated.
Step 8 uses exactness of constant realization on the short exact sequence of coefficient modules; no assertion about completeness or local models is inferred from this generic tool.
Step 7 may equivalently construct the compatible sequence using the stated nonempty-limit theorem on the fibers of the stable-image systems; the proof also spells out their surjectivity.
Step 3 applies the generic site theorem to A/J^n and its nilpotent ideal J/J^n. It supplies lissity only; perfect constancy is supplied separately.
Step 4 uses the existence of affine covering objects weakly contractible in the full pro-etale site, needed for simultaneous constancy and exact evaluation.
Steps 6 and 7 use exact module-sheaf evaluation at the chosen covering object. This gives projective free sheaves and lifts the Milnor epimorphism on sections.
Steps 2, 5, 7 and 8 use functorial Roos derived limits and their exactness; the local-lifting compatibility argument remains in the present item.
Steps 2 and 3 use the canonical tensor comparison for restriction and geometric stalks to retain the quotient normalizations. No proper-base-change or finite-coefficient theorem is used.
Step 4 uses the generic algebraic inverse-limit theorem over the complete ring A for the normalized tower of perfect stalk complexes. It supplies no sheaf trivialization.
Step 5 uses completeness of bounded complexes whose terms are inverse limits of power-torsion sheaves, applied to the explicit idempotent summands defining B tensor P.
Steps 2 and 7 use exact countable products of modules over any pro-etale ring sheaf; this is the generic site input for the Roos and Milnor calculations.
Step 2 identifies the slice at an open chart with its own pro-etale site and preserves the coefficient sheaves. The proof writes out the restriction and product argument.
